questions.question: What is a body fossil? Give four examples.
questions.expected_answer: A body fossil is an actual part of the body of a plant or animal that has been preserved, usually by turning to stone. Examples are teeth, bones, shells, leaves, seeds and petrified wood.

questions.question: What is a trace fossil? Give four examples.
questions.expected_answer: A trace fossil is a sign that a living thing left behind while it was alive, showing what it did, rather than a part of its body. Examples are footprints and tracks, nests, eggs, burrows and droppings.

questions.question: Explain what body fossils and trace fossils can tell scientists.
questions.expected_answer: Body fossils show what living things looked like, their size and shape, and teeth show their diet: sharp teeth for meat-eaters and flat teeth for plant-eaters. Trace fossils show how they lived: footprints show their size, whether they walked or ran, how many legs they walked on and whether they moved in groups; nests and eggs show how they bred; and droppings show what they ate.
